The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. All three lodash calls now map to es-toolkit functions, and the exported signatures are unchanged. The new file type-checks and matches lodash-equivalent behaviour on the example inputs and 3,000 random cases in each stated range.

**What changed**
- `mapValues` → `es-toolkit/object/mapValues`, with the same callback shape.
- `keyBy(rows, 'name')` → `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)`. This is the only adapter, since es-toolkit takes a key function rather than a property name. Last row wins for duplicate names, as in lodash.
- `sortedUniq` → `es-toolkit/array/uniq`. es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. `uniq` keeps first occurrences, so on sorted input it returns the same values.
- Imports use per-function subpaths so the bundle contains only what is used. I did not write any replacement logic by hand.

**Checks**
- **Type check:** `out/module.ts` has no errors. `tsc -p tsconfig.json` still reports errors in `src/module.ts`, the original file. Those are the lodash imports, which can't resolve because lodash isn't installed. I left `src/module.ts` untouched.
- **Results:** The example inputs and 3,000 random cases per function match the reference logic. The reference is written inline in my scratch test, not taken from lodash itself, because lodash isn't installed here.
- **Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 238 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of your own code. I could not measure the original, because the size script fails on the lodash imports without lodash installed. So the "within a small allowance" check can't be confirmed here.

- The skill text I was given was a generic migration guide that says it contains no es-toolkit knowledge. I worked from the es-toolkit package's own declarations and source instead.
- Nothing was installed. I only created the `out/` directory and the scratch test files in the session scratchpad.
